q: How does a trigeneration plant change my Scope 1 and Scope 2?
title: Trigeneration: Scope 1 and 2
short: A gas engine making power, heat and chilled water raises Scope 1, because you now burn the gas yourself, and lowers Scope 2, because you buy less grid power. Whether the total falls depends on how much heat and cooling you actually use. Report both scopes, never just the net.
audience: Hospitals, hotels, malls and process plants

ul: Gas burned in the engine: Scope 1.
Absorption chiller replaces electric chillers, so Scope 2 falls further.
Use metered power, heat and cooling, not nameplate figures.
Low heat use in the off-season can make the plant worse than the grid.
Allocate emissions to power, heat and cooling with one stated method.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices and electricity bills and applies IPCC 2006 factors and the CEA grid factor (0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25), so you can compare Scope 1 and 2 before and after a change from the documents themselves.
